items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: Johnny Hodges is one of them. And so many I know that’s one of them, that are gifted and play.

ctx.x: Oh, that is great. That is great.

So study that’s all. Other people, I know jazz musicians that try to tell some of the young guys they tell them nonsense I call it, they say, “oh man when you study too much it takes away from playing.” That’s the biggest lie that they ever heard of. There’s no such thing as study taking away from anything. I don’t care — I know there are guys that are gifted. Johnny Hodges is one of them. And so many I know that’s one of them, that are gifted and play. See but it’s nothing better than study. Know what you’re…

more you study the better you get. To prove it, some of the greatest musicians that we have in jazz are guys who have studied also. We have some that didn’t okay. But that’s my idea, I say study, you know, that’s what I would say. Study harmonies, you know so you know what you’re doing, see? The more harmonies you know the more you can place them, you know?

Well, I could improvise, I always could improvise. I mean I knew harmony from, just from natural ability, I always could improvise. See, that's why I didn't like to - I was glad to be with this band because I had a chance to, more so than with my brother, all those dance bands. Dance band is commercial gig, you just play the music where it is and you get paid, but I mean, even big bands you don't - even big bands, that's, I'm sure of this, but I'm pretty sure a lot of these fine saxophonists, jazz men who left…

number had something there for tenor, see. But otherwise you don't get a chance to play. That's why Procope went back musically, I mean as far as choruses are concerned, on his horns. Procope was a great saxophone player then, on the period he was working with Kirby, you understand? But when he worked with these big bands playing first, he didn't get the chance, there was too many others. When this is, like Johnny Hodg[es] and those guys, they would favor them, see, so he didn't have a chance to play as much. So…
Yeah. So we have you - well, wait a second, you made the comment yesterday when we were talking about blues singer over at the radio station -

items.q: like Johnny Hod[ges] and so many others.

ctx.x: So I'm trying to figure out, you know, how good and how special this was, that you're saying that they're bands in 1918 were playing solos.

I was playing solos, that's what I'm say- I was playing solos, you know what I mean? See, but I was playing solos on the chords in the same principle that I play solos on the chords now, you see what I mean? See, to improvise you have to know the harmony, one way or the other. Either you're gonna study, or from natural ability, like Johnny Hod[ges] and so many others. One way you got that, [ ], so after you know the harmony, you can play the chords. A chord has, if you have a seven chord you have 4 notes in it. A…
